message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic and modern horror films across various sub‑genres—so you’ll have something whether you’re into psychological dread, supernatural chills, or gore‑heavy thrills:

| # | Title | Year | Sub‑genre | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Psychological / Gothic | Kubrick’s masterful build‑up of isolation and madness; iconic imagery. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Supernatural / Family trauma | A fresh take on inherited curses with bone‑shaking performances. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Social satire / Thriller | Horror meets sharp commentary on race; clever plot twists. |
| 4 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Folk horror | Daylight terror in a Swedish festival; unsettling atmosphere. |
| 5 | **It Follows** | 2014 | Urban legend / Slow‑burn | Simple premise but effective paranoia; great soundtrack. |
| 6 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Survival / Sci‑fi | Silence as a weapon; tense family dynamics. |
| 7 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Psychological / Mythic creature | Metaphor for grief; haunting score. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | Paranormal investigation | Well‑crafted scares, grounded characters. |
| 9 | **Suspiria (1977)** | 1977 | Giallo / Dance | Visually striking, eerie soundtrack; cult status. |
|10 | **The Witch** | 2015 | Period horror | Creepy authenticity, slow‑burn dread. |

If you want more recommendations tailored to a specific mood (e.g., “gore‑heavy” vs. “psychological”), just let me know!
